# PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT] Contents of this Part

## Scope and interpretation

## 75.1

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (1) Practice Direction 75 –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (a) sets out the proceedings to which this Part applies; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (b) may apply this Part with modifications in relation to any particular category of those proceedings.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (Rule 21.1(1)(c)(i) provides that Part 21 (children and protected parties) does not apply to proceedings under this Part where one of the parties is a child.)

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (2) In this Part –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (a) ‘the Centre’ means the Traffic Enforcement Centre established under the direction of the Lord Chancellor;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (a1) ‘enforcement agent’ has the meaning given in paragraph 2(1) of Schedule 12 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007(1);

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (a2) ‘local authority warrant of control’ means a warrant of control issued by a local authority under article 5 of the 1993 Order;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (b) ‘no relevant return to the warrant’ means that –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (i) the enforcement agent has been unable to seize goods because the enforcement agent has been denied access to premises occupied by the defendant or because the goods have been removed from those premises;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (ii) any goods seized under a local authority warrant of control are insufficient to satisfy the debt and the cost of execution; or

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (iii) the goods are insufficient to cover the cost of their removal and sale;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (c) ‘the 1993 Order’ means the Enforcement of Road Traffic Debts Order 1993;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (d) ‘relevant period’, in relation to any particular case, means –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (i) the period allowed for serving a statutory declaration or witness statement under any enactment which applies to that case; or

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (ii) where an enactment permits the court to extend that period, the period as extended;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (e) ‘specified debts’ means the debts specified in article 2 of the 1993 Order or treated as so specified by any other enactment; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.1] (f) ‘the authority’, ‘notice of the amount due’, ‘order’ and ‘the respondent’ have the meaning given by Practice Direction 75.

## The centre

## 75.2

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.2] (1) Proceedings to which this Part applies must be started in the Centre.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.2] (2) For any purpose connected with the exercise of the Centre’s functions –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.2] (a) the Centre is deemed to be an office of the County Court; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.2] (b) any officer of the Centre, in exercising its functions, is deemed to act as an officer of the County Court.

## Request

## 75.3

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (1) The authority must file a request in the appropriate form scheduling the amount claimed to be due.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (2) The authority must, in that request or in another manner approved by the court officer

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (a) certify –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (i) that 14 days have elapsed since service of the notice of the amount due;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (ii) the date of such service;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (iii) the number of the notice of the amount due; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (iv) that the amount due remains unpaid;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (b) specify the grounds (whether by reference to the appropriate code or otherwise), as stated in the notice, on which the authority claims to be entitled to claim that amount; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (c) state –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (i) the name, title and address of the respondent;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (ii) the registration number of the vehicle concerned;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (iii) the authority’s address for service;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (iv) the court fee; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (v) such other matters as required by Practice Direction 75.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (3) On receipt of a request that meets the requirements of paragraphs (1) and (2), the court officer will order that the amount due may be recovered as if it were payable under a County Court order by registering the request and returning it to the authority.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (4) On receipt of a registered request the authority may draw up the order and must –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (a) insert in the order the date by which the respondent must either –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (i) comply with the order; or

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (ii) file a statutory declaration or witness statement; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (b) attach to the order a form of statutory declaration or witness statement for the respondent’s use.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.3] (5) The authority must serve in accordance with Part 6 the order (and the form of statutory declaration or witness statement) on the respondent within 15 days of the date on which the request is registered by the court.

## Electronic delivery of documents

## 75.4

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.4] (1) Where the authority is required to file any document other than the request, that requirement is satisfied if the information which would be contained in the document is delivered in computer-readable form.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.4] (2) For the purposes of paragraph (1), information which would be contained in a document relating to one case may be combined with information of the same nature relating to another case.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.4] (3) Where a document is required to be produced, that requirement will be satisfied if a copy of the document is produced from computer records.

## Functions of court officer

## 75.5

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5] (1) Practice Direction 75 sets out the circumstances in which a court officer may exercise the functions of the court.

## Review of decision of court officer

## 75.5A

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] (1) Any party may request any decision of a court officer to be reviewed by a district judge.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] (2) Such a request must be made within 14 days of service of the decision.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] (3) Unless –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] (a) the party requesting the review requests an oral hearing; or

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] (b) the court orders an oral hearing,

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.5A] a request for a review under paragraph (2) will be dealt with without an oral hearing.

## Enforcement of orders

## 75.6

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] Subject to the 1993 Order and this rule the following rules apply to the enforcement of specified debts –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] (a) Parts 70 to 73;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] (b) CCR Order 25, rule 1;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] (c) rule 83.2;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] (ca) rule 83.4; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.6] (d) Part 89.

## Warrant of execution

## 75.7

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (1) An authority seeking the issue of a local authority warrant of control must file a request –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (a) certifying the amount remaining due under the order;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (b) specifying the date of service of the order on the respondent; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (c) certifying that the relevant period has elapsed.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (2) The court will seal the request and return it to the authority.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (3) Within 7 days of the sealing of the request the authority must prepare the warrant in the appropriate form.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (4) No payment under a warrant will be made to the court.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (5) For the purposes of execution a warrant will be valid for 12 months beginning with the date of its issue.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (6) An authority may not renew a warrant issued in accordance with this Part beyond the 12 month validity period but, subject to paragraph (7), an authority may request the reissue of a warrant during the 12 month validity period.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (7) Where the address of the respondent has changed since the issue of the warrant, the authority may request the reissue of the warrant by filing a request –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (a) specifying the new address of the respondent;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (b) providing evidence that the new address for the respondent does relate to the respondent named in the order and against whom enforcement is sought; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (c) certifying that the amount due under the order remains unpaid.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (8) Where the court is satisfied that the new address of the respondent given in the request for the reissue of the warrant relates to the respondent named in the order, it will seal the request and return it to the authority.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (9) The authority must prepare the reissued warrant in the appropriate form within 7 days of the sealing of the request to reissue.

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.7] (10) A reissued warrant will only be valid for the remainder of the 12 month period beginning with the date it was originally issued.

## Revocation of order

## 75.8

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.8] Where, in accordance with any enactment, an order is deemed to have been revoked following the filing of a statutory declaration or a witness statement –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.8] (a) the court will serve a copy of the statutory declaration or witness statement on the authority;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.8] (b) any execution issued on the order will cease to have effect; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.8] (c) if appropriate, the authority must inform any enforcement agent instructed to levy execution of the withdrawal of the warrant as soon as possible.

## Transfer for enforcement

## 75.9

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.9] Where the authority requests the transfer of proceedings to a County Court hearing centre for enforcement, the request must –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.9] (a) where the authority has not attempted to enforce by execution, give the reason why no such attempt was made;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.9] (b) certify that there has been no relevant return to the local authority warrant of control;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.9] (c) specify the date of service of the order on the respondent; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.9] (d) certify that the relevant period has elapsed.

## Further information required

## 75.10

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] An application for –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (a) an attachment of earnings order;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (b) an order to obtain information from a debtor;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (c) a third party debt order; or

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (d) a charging order,

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] must, in addition to the requirements of Parts 71, 72, 73 or 89 –

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (i) where the authority has not attempted to enforce by execution, give the reason why no such attempt was made;

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (ii) certify that there has been no relevant return to the local authority warrant of control

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (iii) specify the date of service of the order on the respondent; and

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.10] (iv) certify that the relevant period has elapsed.

## Combining requests

## 75.11

[PART 75 – TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT > 75.11] Where the court officer allows, the authority may combine information relating to different orders against the same respondent in any request or application made under rules 75.9 or 75.10.
